COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
UKHC010196652026
WPSS/2849/2026
Renu Rautela
--Petitioner
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. G.S. Negi, learned Addl. C.S.C. for the State.
3. Mr. Ramji Shrivastava, learned counsel for the 
respondent no. 3.
4. The order impugned passed by the Director is 
apparently in complete defiance of the order of the 
writ court dated 25.08.2025 passed in bunch of 
petitions, the leading one is WPSS No. 483 of 2024, as 
well as another judgment of the Coordinate 
Bench dated 22.09.2025 passed in bunch of petitions, 
the leading one is WPSS No. 494 of 2024.
5. Both these two judgments relates to the 
advertisement in which the petitioner participate. 
Surprisingly, the Director by the impugned order by 
taking cognizance of another judgment which has 
nothing to do with the advertisement rejected the 
representation of the petitioner and refused to grant 
relaxation.
6. In such view of the matter, post this matter on 
05.11.2026.
7. The Director shall join the proceeding through 
V.C. and justify his stand in rejecting representation 
which appears be in complete defiance of the order of 
the writ court. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 03.11.2026
PR

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
UKHC010196652026
WPSS/2849/2026
Renu Rautela
--Petitioner
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. G.S. Negi, learned Addl. Chief Standing
Counsel for the State.
3. Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel for the
respondents. 
4. Mr. Ashutosh Sayana, Director, joined the
proceeding through V.C.
5. Order impugned has been passed in complete
defiance of the order dated 25.08.2025 passed by the
Coordinate Bench in WPSS No. 483 of 2024, the
operative portion of which is being reproduced as
under:
“26. All the writ petitions are allowed. Pursuant to
the advertisement dated 11.03.2024 of the Board, the cut off
date for determining the age of the petitioners shall be
01.07.2020. By the interim orders of this Court, all the
petitioners were permitted to participate in the recruitment
process, but it was directed to the Board that their result
shall not be declared. Now, in view of this judgment, the
Board shall declare the result of the petitioners.”
6. It reveals that the impugned order has been
passed by the Director taking note of the another order
passed by the Writ Court in WPSS No. 2126 of 2025
which has nothing to do with the selection, in
question. Now, the question, how the Director has
passed the impugned order in defiance of the order passed by the writ Court. It appears that the action of
the Director while issuing impugned order appears to
be contemptuous, therefore, this Court has no option
except to invoke powers under Article 215 of the
Constitution of India. However, before taking steps
under Article 215 of the Constitution of India, ten days
time is granted to the Director to file his response.
7. List on 18.11.2026.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 05.11.2026
SKS

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
UKHC010196652026
WPSS/2849/2026
Renu Rautela --Petitioner
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand --Respondent
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. G.S. Negi, learned Addl. CSC for the 
State of Uttarakhand.
3. Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel for the 
respondents.
4. Admittedly the order impugned whereby 
the claim of the petitioner for seeking age 
relaxation has been rejected without gone through 
with the judgment of the writ court dated 
25.08.2025 passed in bunch of writ petitions 
leading one is WPSS No.483 of 2024 “Abhilasha 
Saxena and others Vs. State of Uttarakhand and 
others”.
5. It appears that the official respondent who 
pass the order impugned have not applied their
mind. At this juncture, the operative part of the 
order of the writ court dated 25.08.2025, is being 
extracted hereinasunder:-
“26. All the writ petitions are allowed. Pursuant to 
the advertisement dated 11.03.2024 of the Board, the 
cut off date for determining the age of the petitioners 
shall be 01.07.2020. By the interim orders of this 
Court, all the petitioners were permitted to participate 
in the recruitment process, but it was directed to the 
Board that their result shall not be declared. Now, in 
view of this judgment, the Board shall declare the 
result of the petitioners.”
6. As per the order of the writ court, 01.07.2020
was fixed as cut off date for determination of the 
age. Taking the parity of this judgment, the 
petitioner also filed a writ petition, but the same  was dismissed, and then he filed the special appeal 
and ultimately the special appeal was disposed of
finally and liberty was granted to the petitioner to 
move a representation for age relaxation and 
pursuant to such a liberty, he made a 
representation to the Director, but the 
representation has been rejected by taking note of
an another order of the writ court which has 
nothing to do with this selection in which the 
petitioner participate, which shows that the 
Director has not applied its mind at all and 
completely overlooked the judicial verdict of the 
writ court dated 25.08.2025 passed in bunch of writ 
petitions. The official respondent has no 
authority to bye-pass a judicial verdict and they 
have to obey it in letter and spirit. 
7. The Director joins the proceeding through 
VC and apologise for the mistake which he has 
committed while rejecting representation and 
undertakes that he will take a decision afresh. Let 
he may take a fresh decision positively within a 
week, and then apprise to the Court on the next 
date.
8. Put up this matter on 30.11.2026.
9. The personal appearance of the Official is 
exempted for the time being. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 18.11.2026
Nitesh/
